visual.general_description: Two grayscale CT images of the head shown side by side: a coronal image through the paranasal sinuses on the left and an axial image at the level of the nose and skull base on the right.
visual.detailed_description: Left image (coronal): printed orientation letters H at the top, F at the bottom, R at the left edge and L at the right edge. The cranial vault and brain parenchyma fill the upper half, the orbits sit at the sides, and below them the nasal cavity, ethmoid region and both maxillary sinuses are shown. The large black cavities on both sides below the orbits have intermediate gray areas along their lower walls, larger on the image-right side, and the central region between them shows intermediate gray areas with small black air pockets and thin bony partitions. A bright horizontal streak with dark bands crosses the image at the level of the lower face. Right image (axial, bone-type window): printed letters A at the top, P at the bottom, R at the left and L at the right. The nose with a midline septum and both nasal passages is at the top, the maxillary sinuses are visible anterolaterally with black air, and in the posterior part bone on both sides behind the ears shows a honeycomb pattern of small black spaces; the back of the head rests on a curved support. No arrows, measurements, panel letters, patient name text or numeric overlays are visible in either image.

clinical_significance.statement: The article presents the CT as supporting the clinical findings of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, with septal, ostiomeatal complex, ethmoid and mucosal findings stated in the text.

evidence.quote: A CT scan supported the clinical findings, showing a left septal spur, right-sided polypoid changes involving the ostiomeatal complex, bilateral chronic ethmoid sinus fullness, and bilateral obstruction of the ostiomeatal complexes.
Additional findings included mucosal thickening of the maxillary, sphenoid, and frontal sinuses (Figure 1).

limitations: The two images are unlettered; "left" and "right" image positions are positions only. Disease extent and the septal findings stated in the caption are author statements and are not independently determined from the pixels.
Two unlettered images in one file; described as one whole-figure panel.
